justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a relatively stable near-term outlook with modest upward drift over time. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of 978 likely anchors closely to the most recent observed value, assuming mean-reverting dynamics and no major scheduled catalysts within the next trading session. The slight upward drift to 985 at one week and 995 at one month reflects a mild positive trend assumption — perhaps a modest growth or recovery bias baked into the underlying series — while acknowledging that the series does not appear to be in a strongly trending regime at the moment.

Confidence interval widths widen appropriately as the horizon extends, reflecting the compounding of uncertainty over time. At one day, the 90% interval of roughly plus or minus 27 points is relatively tight, consistent with typical short-term volatility in a series of this magnitude. By one month, the interval spans about 230 points, which reflects not just volatility accumulation but also structural uncertainty — we cannot reliably predict how macroeconomic conditions, policy signals, or sentiment shifts will evolve over a four-week window. The asymmetry in the intervals is fairly modest, suggesting I did not have strong skew assumptions in either direction.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside these stated intervals include sudden macroeconomic shocks such as an unexpected inflation print, central bank policy surprise, or geopolitical escalation. On the upside, a stronger-than-expected data release or positive policy development could push the series well above the upper bound of the one-month interval. Structural breaks — such as a sudden liquidity event or a sentiment cascade — are particularly hard to model and represent the most likely mechanism for outcomes falling in the tails beyond my stated 90% bounds. These tail scenarios, by construction, have roughly a 10% combined probability but can be disproportionately impactful when they materialize.
